01 — The Format

Friends Keep Secrets meets Chicken Shop Date

One host, one special guest, one table. Unscripted conversation about anything — no topic off limits. TDTM borrows its intimacy from one show and its setting-as-hook from the other.

What TDTM borrows: the candor. Unscripted, celebrity-comfortable conversation — guests who wouldn't normally open up, actually opening up.

×

What TDTM borrows: the venue-as-hook. One specific, recognizable table as the whole set. The location does half the marketing.

TDTM at Pawn Shop is both of these at once — except it’s live, it’s sports, and the audience is in the room.

TDTM Proof of Concept

The Adrian Gonzalez Episode

Adrian Gonzalez is a former Dodgers first baseman who owns two restaurants in Los Angeles. Melissa filmed his podcast episode on location — kitchen walkthrough, promo videos, two locations in one day. The episode cost approximately $2,500 out of pocket and came out at a level the show hadn’t reached before. The format worked because the restaurant was not the backdrop. It was the point.

Watch on YouTube ↗

At Pawn Shop, it goes further.

    The room and the internet get the same moment at the same time — the audience isn’t capped at the door.

02 — The Opportunity

Not Just a Podcast. Revenue-Driving Events.

One event type sells a premium menu. The other sells the ticket itself. Both create incremental revenue and give TDTM’s audience a new reason to experience Pawn Shop in person.

01PILLAR 01

Special-Guest Live Podcast + Event

A ticketed taping with a live audience and a curated, renamed TDTM × Pawn Shop menu, priced above the regular check.

  • ✦2–3 food items, 2–3 drinks, collab-branded
  • ✦Premium pricing lifts average check
  • ✦Revenue split on the premium, not the base menu
02PILLAR 02

Ticketed Dodgers Watch Parties

Limited-capacity private rooms for live Dodgers games — exclusive, social, with guests ordering freely from the full Pawn Shop menu. The ticket is the experience.

  • ✦Capped headcount keeps it feeling exclusive
  • ✦On-site catering + bartender, built into the price
  • ✦100% of ticket revenue is incremental

What TDTM Takes Home

Launch nights

Without Alcohol Sponsor

Food premium

~$300 per night

TDTM takes the $2 above standard Pawn Shop prices on each collab food item. Pawn Shop keeps their full normal margin on every dish. The $2 is the only difference.

Named cocktail share

~$125 per night

Extra Innings and The 7th Inning are net new drinks with no existing Pawn Shop price. TDTM takes 20% of revenue from those two drinks only — not the full bar. Pawn Shop keeps 80% plus full margin on every other drink ordered.

TDTM total per night~$400 to $425

The $400 formalizes the partnership. TDTM’s real return is the filmed content, guest relationship, and brand exposure to 75 people in the room.

Preferred scenario

With Alcohol Sponsor

Sponsor fee

$2,000 to $5,000 per event

A brand — a tequila label, Modelo, a wine partner — pays a flat fee to have their product featured in the cocktails, named in the menu, and promoted by Melissa on camera and across social content after the night.

Cocktail split

Waived

With a sponsor in place, TDTM takes nothing from bar revenue. Pawn Shop keeps 100% of all cocktail and bar income. The sponsor fee replaces the split entirely.

Food premium

~$300 per night

Same as without a sponsor — TDTM keeps the $2 above standard price on collab food items only.

TDTM total per night$2,300 to $5,300

Mookie Betts is the natural first sponsor conversation: his tequila is already poured at Pawn Shop. Featuring it in the Extra Innings cocktail gives his brand YouTube and social exposure, TDTM a sponsor fee, and Pawn Shop every bar dollar.

The first nights launch without a sponsor. The sponsor conversation starts the same week.

06 — Why Pawn Shop, Specifically

The fit already exists

This isn’t a cold pitch to a random restaurant — Pawn Shop already sits inside the TDTM world.

01

Already on the menu

Mookie Betts's tequila is poured at Pawn Shop today, and he's said to be an investor. The Dodgers connection isn't a pitch — it's already behind the bar.

02

Melrose is the right room

A high-visibility LA location built for a crowd that photographs and posts — exactly the audience a live-taped, social-first podcast needs in the room.

03

Distribution Pawn Shop doesn't have to build

Every episode lives on YouTube and social after the night ends — the restaurant is on camera for an audience far bigger than the room itself.
